pilot.title: Discord rules audit pilot
pilot.coverage_note: All 1,129 messages in the inclusive pilot window were reviewed, with source checks and attachment evidence. No additional genuine missing rule, contradiction or verified fix qualified. The colored reference notes below come from the existing register outside the pilot dates; their dates and authority are shown. Older source editions and later local v4.3.1 sheets are distinguished.

annotations.title: Airborne sequence: one combined Fighter/AAA step
annotations.body: In the developer’s posted v4.4 correction, both sides’ Fighters and AAA resolve in step 4, once. Step 5 moves surviving transports to a suitable landing spot. Airborne infantry and its transporting aircraft remain linked as one casualty through steps 3 and 4; destroyed cargo does not land or attack. This correction is applied to this project at the user’s request.
annotations.author: Global War ’36 Enthusiast
annotations.authority_detail: Rule image inspected directly in Discord. It is explicitly a v4.4 correction, applied here; the baseline PDF remains v4.3.

annotations.title: Foreign-invasion alignment: the whole warlord aligns
annotations.body: The entire warlord aligns: one alignment roll per whole warlord decides all its remaining territories and forces. Determine neighboring factions across the whole warlord. Beiping/Hopeh and Kwangtung/Hainan each remain one warlord. This settles the table’s “For each land zone” wording in favour of the whole-warlord description above it.
annotations.authority_detail: Reported by the user on 22 November 2026; the user had adopted the same reading on 5 October 2026. Retains the source table’s automatic outcomes; does not turn individual provinces into separate warlords.

annotations.title: CCP purchases: railroad wording, not a generic supply path
annotations.body: Use the undamaged railroad connection from CCP-possessed land to Soviet-possessed land required by Comintern Brothers, including its placement restriction. A sea-only or river-only supply path does not unlock these Artillery/AAA purchases. The user reports that the developers fixed the inconsistent purchase-note wording for the next version.
annotations.authority_detail: Reported developer resolution; a subsequently published replacement sheet has not been verified here.

annotations.title: Enemy presence preventing a blockade
annotations.body: Only enemy Surface Warships prevent a blockade under the enemy-presence condition. Enemy submarines alone do not prevent an otherwise qualifying surface fleet from blockading. Retain all fleet-size, alliance and sea-access requirements.
annotations.authority_detail: Resolves the broader naval-summary wording against the detailed blockade rule; direct message link was not supplied with the report.

annotations.title: Japanese border-clash targets
annotations.body: Project ruling: treat Japan’s reference-sheet target list as exhaustive. Japan may target Soviet units in Chita, Amur and Primorsky Krai; Soviet possession elsewhere does not expand that list. Keep the ordinary border-clash eligibility, one-round and no-conquest restrictions.
annotations.authority_detail: This choice reconciles the general geography with Japan’s national list; it does not add USSR attack origins.

annotations.title: Dadao lend-lease destination
annotations.body: Project ruling pending developer clarification: Japanese lend-lease may be delivered to any Dadao-possessed land within Chinese Home Country, subject to all ordinary supply-route, timing, blockade and item limits. This supplies a destination for the explicit aid permission when Dadao has no original Home Country; it does not redefine Dadao’s Home Country for other rules.
annotations.authority_detail: Genuine missing delivery destination; no developer ruling has been reported.

annotations.title: Chinese Truce: attacker and defender
annotations.body: When CCP or KMT breaks the Truce on its own turn, that active faction attacks. When a third party triggers evolution and automatic termination, the possessor of each shared land zone defends and the other Chinese faction attacks.
annotations.authority_detail: Third-party roles are a developer ruling reported by the user. Ordinary own-turn roles also follow the rulebook and the separately linked June discussion in the register.

annotations.title: Chinese Truce: Low Morale after automatic termination
annotations.body: Project ruling: use the same normal-attack-roll 10+ elimination for eligible attacking minor-KMT regular Infantry/Cavalry in shared zones after voluntary or automatic termination. There is no additional preliminary roll. Defending KMT and Major-Power KMT remain exempt.
annotations.authority_detail: The automatic-termination Low Morale extension is the user’s choice, separately identified from the developer’s attacker/defender clarification.

annotations.title: Advanced Artillery city bombardment conditions
annotations.body: Project ruling: city bombardment uses attrition’s starting-adjacency and no-movement conditions. The gun remains in its original zone and fires at a city adjacent since the Player Turn began. City bombardment still deals 1D6 strategic damage; it does not use attrition’s hit-at-2 attack against units.
annotations.authority_detail: Ordinary attrition’s own restrictions are already explicit. This note concerns their extension to city bombardment only.

annotations.title: Port evacuation into a third party’s enemy fleet
annotations.body: When damaged-port evacuation forces combat with an enemy fleet, the evacuating fleet defends and the fleet already at sea attacks, even during a third nation's turn. This developer clarification replaces the earlier provisional project ruling.
annotations.authority_detail: Source: user-provided Discord screenshot, 23 October 2026; direct message link not supplied. The example has Commonwealth ships defending against Italian ships during German bombing. The campaign applies the same roles to three-alliance cases; that exact example was not in the message.
annotations.author: The Warden

annotations.title: Required neutral relocation without a Friendly destination
annotations.body: Provisional project ruling: eliminate nonparticipating neutral units required to relocate after conquest only when no Friendly relocation destination exists. Where a destination exists, retain the printed nearest-Friendly-land rule regardless of distance.
annotations.authority_detail: The user adopted the proposed no-destination consequence for now on 23 October 2026. The source permits neutral co-occupants but does not specify this elimination consequence; developer clarification is still pending.

annotations.title: Low Morale with no legal retreat
annotations.body: Developer clarification: an attacking minor-KMT regular Infantry or Cavalry unit that rolls 10+ but cannot retreat to the zone it attacked from, such as one landed in an amphibious assault, is eliminated. A unit that can retreat to its attack origin still does so.
annotations.authority_detail: The user reported on 21 November 2026 that the developers clarified the rule this way; no message link was supplied. The user had adopted the same ruling on 2 November 2026: the source does not say what happens when the Low Morale retreat is impossible, and the ruling followed the city and tundra/ice rules, which eliminate attackers that must retreat but cannot.

annotations.title: A patrol plane's second chance against ships it let pass
annotations.body: Project ruling, revised: a patrol plane that lets ships without attacking aircraft pass shares its sea zone with them. It takes no part in their screening battle or the battle where their route ends, and it does not stop their amphibious assaults. They may still attack it anew in Combat Movement; it then chooses again by the patrol rule, before any scramble, and once it has fought it stops their amphibious assault if it survives.
annotations.authority_detail: The user first adopted the one-decision reading on 4 November 2026, after the question was found in random-play seed 9487, and reversed it the same day. RB 0.3 lists a declined patrol among the ways units at war share a sea zone, which lasts until one power makes a new combat move against the other units there; RB 9.4.2 and 10.8.1 exempt an aircraft on MAP which declined combat.

annotations.title: Amphibious assault from an uncleared sea zone
annotations.body: Project ruling: if Enemy surface ships or aircraft remain in the assault's sea zone after its naval combat, such as ships scrambled into it, or its transports retreat, the amphibious assault is called off and its land units stay aboard for the rest of the turn. The assault still goes ahead with any cargo whose transports remain in the cleared sea zone.
annotations.authority_detail: The user adopted this on 3 November 2026. RB 10.8.1 requires those units to be eliminated first and lets defenders scramble, but does not say what happens when they survive; found as a self-play dead end on 2 November 2026.

annotations.title: One railroad per border, damaged and repaired by side
annotations.body: Project ruling: a border has at most one railroad, so building one is not offered where a railroad, damaged or not, already exists or is under construction. Each side of the border holds its own damage, up to 1 in normal terrain and 2 in difficult terrain; a railroad damaged on either side cannot be used, and the nation possessing a damaged side's zone repairs that side at 1 IPP per point.
annotations.authority_detail: The user confirmed the per-side damage and repair on 3 November 2026; on 4 November 2026 the user confirmed 2 damage per side in difficult terrain and adopted one railroad per border as an equivalence ruling: bombing damages every railroad on a border together (RB 10.6.2), and repairing both sides at their maximum costs the building price.

annotations.title: A patrol plane attacked in its own sea zone
annotations.body: Project ruling: when ships already in its sea zone attack a patrol plane, it chooses by the patrol rule, not the carrier rule. It may stay out unless the Attacker has aircraft with an attack value present, and staying out costs it nothing. It chooses before any scramble: if it stays out and nothing else of its side defends, there is no battle and nothing to scramble into. A plane that stays out has declined combat again and does not count against their screening or amphibious assault. Nothing scrambles into the single round it fights against entering units during Combat Movement.
annotations.authority_detail: The user adopted this on 4 November 2026. The rulebook gives a patrol plane's choice only for ships entering its zone, and the naval combat sequence puts scrambles before the choice of aircraft on carriers; the engine had given patrol planes that carrier choice.

annotations.title: An attack on land that was Chinese at the start
annotations.body: Developer clarification reported by the user: an attack by a nation that is not Chinese on a land zone that was originally a warlord's, the CCP's or the KMT's declares war on all of China whoever holds the zone now, or if nobody does; a zone the Dadao Government holds is the one exception. The attack puts the attacker at war with the KMT, the CCP and every warlord not yet aligned, except a nation of its own alliance, and any nation that is not Chinese may make it, Mongolia too. So Mongolia's attack puts it at war with the KMT and those warlords, never with the CCP, and in the full game an attack by a nation of the Allies never puts it at war with the KMT. Read here: Mongolia still attacks only a zone whose holder it is already at war with, or one nobody holds (4.5).
annotations.authority_detail: The user reported the developers' answer on 22 November 2026, answering the project's questions Q-001 and Q-002. It replaces the user's reading of 19 November 2026, under which rules 4.5 and 5.1 forbade the attack to Mongolia.

annotations.title: A land battle that no unit can end
annotations.body: Project ruling: when no unit of either side could roll a die in the next combat round, the battle could never end by fighting, and the attacker retreats as its only action. Its units that may retreat go back as in any retreat; its units with nowhere to go, those that came from the sea or by air drop and land units with no Friendly zone to go back to, are eliminated, and the defender keeps the zone. A retreat by choice that leaves only units that came from the sea or by air drop eliminates them at once when no unit of either side could roll in the next round. Every other battle keeps the printed rules: such units stay and fight on while some unit can still roll.
annotations.authority_detail: The user adopted this on 22 November 2026, answering the project's question Q-014: "Let's say the player is allowed to retreat as an action and if the unit has nowhere to go that unit dies." The rulebook repeats the combat rounds until the battle is over and gives a printed end for attackers that must retreat and cannot only in a city, after three rounds, and on tundra or ice, after one (1.7.7, 1.7.5).

annotations.title: Two attacks on one land zone by a controlled Minor Power and its controller
annotations.body: Project ruling: of the nations that share a Player Turn, a controlled Minor Power and its Controlling Major Power, only the first to attack a land zone may attack it in that turn. The other may not attack it overland or across a strait, from the sea, by air drop, with aircraft, by blitzing or by an attrition attack, and an aircraft supports only a battle of its own nation. The first may add attacks of its own, and the zone is open to both again in their next Player Turn. An attack counts from the moment it is made or declared, even if its battle is lost or its assault is called off; strategic bombing and rocket attacks on facilities, cities or railroads are not attacks on the zone.
annotations.authority_detail: The user adopted this on 24 November 2026, answering the project's question Q-019: "Go with A for Q19". The rulebook says that controlled Minor Powers "may not attack together" with their controller (7.1) and, where it lets two nations attack together, means units of both against one land zone (10.10; Operation Overlord, USA sheet). Found when a training game stopped after Japan and Dadao had both attacked Manchuria-Rehe in one turn.
